newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania slides towards anarchy as looting spreads. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Albania slides towards anarchy as looting spreads. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]

text.p: Albania slid towards anarchy on Thursday as arms depots in several towns including the capital Tirana were looted and people used the weapons to raid food warehouses for emergency stockpiles.

As gunfire crackled around the capital in an orgy of celebration, Tirana airport was closed after a nearby military base was looted, preventing the evacuation of some foreign embassy staff ordered out by their governments.

A European mediation mission headed by former Austrian leader Franz Vranitzky was due to fly into Tirana on Thursday to resume efforts to end the chaos. Vranitzky said he would try to reach the capital later in the day.
In the northern city of Shkoder, until now untouched by the armed rebellion sweeping the country, doctors reported that five people had died and several were wounded as two arms depots were looted.

Unlike rebels who have seized control of the south in an anti-government uprising sparked by anger over the collapse of pyramid savings schemes, looters in the north appeared to be arming themselves for self-protection.
"We are not against the president or the government, we just want to protect ourselves," one man in a village outside the capital said as he shouldered a captured Kalashnikov automatic rifle.

The U.S. military said it had put a naval battle group on standby in the Adriatic Sea in case Washington decided to use troops to evacuate more than 2,000 Americans (corrects from Albanians) living in Albania.
"We are basically in a standby mode," said a spokesman at the U.S. European Command in Stuttgart.

In Athens, the defence ministry said a Greek navy minesweeper was waiting off the coast of the southern Albanian rebel-held port of Sarande until local leaders organised themseves to receive its cargo of food and medicine.
Rebels in the south accuse President Sali Berisha of allowing the schemes to flourish, and of not warning people of the risks, and are demanding he resigns before they hand in their weapons.
As the country plunged into chaos a new all-party government demanded by the rebels, and approved by Berisha on Wednesday, was due to be sworn in on Thursday.

Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, a Socialist from Gjirokaster, one of the southern towns now in rebel hands, said on Wednesday evening: "After consultations with all political forces we have tried to make a government for all Albanians."
"I call on Albanians in these times to think about Albania, not political forces," Fino said, adding that he wanted to open a dialogue with rebels in the south.
In Tirana residents woke on Thursday to find that the military academy and other arms depots in the area had been looted of weapons and other equipment during the night.
Hundreds of civilians, some armed, raided a large Swiss-owned warehouse located in a suburb of Tirana and made off with 650 tonnes of flour in trucks, on donkeys and on bicycles.
Members of the Shik secret police armed with rifles arrived on the scene but left soon afterwards without intervening. There was virtually no uniformed police presence in the city.
Outside the capital the situation was reported to be equally chaotic as arms depots were raided, and virtually all able-bodied men were carrying weapons of some sort, many firing them into the air.
In the town of Lac, 45 kms (30 miles) north of Tirana, a Reuters reporter saw a crowd of several hundred people force the police to release some 40 prisoners from police cells.
The U.S. State Department said on Wednesday it was ordering 160 government employees and their dependents to leave by regular or charter flights. Another 2,000 Americans were urged to go.
A diplomatic source said orders this week by most Western countries to pull out stemmed from "logical safety criteria. They have no reflection on the country or the government."
Bulgaria said on Thursday it had three planes standing by to evacuate some 100 Bulgarian citizens if and when the airport is reopened.
U.S. ambassador Marisa Lino appeared on Albanian television on Wednesdsay urging viewers to back the new government. "You cannot build a democracy by resorting to violence," she said in Albanian.
